headings.text: Base URL & how to call it

blocks.html:
The authoritative reference for everything in this guide is the official TAK Server API spec. Bookmark it:

https://docs.tak.gov/api/takserver

How the spec is published

  • It's rendered with Redoc and is versioned — a dropdown at the top selects the TAK Server build (this guide tracks 5.6-RELEASE-14). Pick the version that matches the server you integrate with; endpoints and fields change between versions.

  • The raw OpenAPI document for a version is fetchable directly — useful for codegen or tooling:

    https://docs.tak.gov/api/takserver/<version>/openapispec.json
# e.g. https://docs.tak.gov/api/takserver/5.6-RELEASE-14/openapispec.json

  • The spec is public (no login needed) and describes ~300 operations, all under /Marti/api/….

Base URL & how to call it

  • Every path is rooted at **/Marti/api/…** on your TAK Server host. The spec's default https://127.0.0.1:17655 is just the local admin example; on a real deployment you call the server's certificate-auth HTTPS port. On a Deploy App / PVARKI deployment that is port **8443**, e.g. https://<server>:8443/Marti/api/… — and the same host:port serves the Mission Manager admin UI at https://<server>:8443/Marti/MissionManager.html.
  • Auth is at the transport layer. Most operations don't show an API key/bearer in the spec because access is granted by your mTLS client certificate (and, where configured, an OAuth/OIDC token). Present your client cert on every request — see Enrolling & getting a client certificate.
  • Responses are JSON; many list endpoints return a { "version", "type", "data": […] } envelope typical of Marti.

Reading the spec efficiently

Group the endpoints by what you're trying to do:

  • Move data with a team → the Missions / Data Sync endpoints (/Marti/api/missions/…). Start here for most integrations.
  • Store/fetch files & data packages → Enterprise Sync (/Marti/api/sync/…, /Marti/api/files/…), addressed by content hash.
  • Live CoT → Subscriptions (/Marti/api/subscriptions/…) plus the streaming port for the actual event flow.
  • Who sees what → Groups (/Marti/api/groups/…).
  • Wire in external sources/sinks → Inputs, Data Feeds, Outgoing connections.

The next two pages walk the common read and write paths; both defer to the spec for the exact request/response shapes and query parameters.
